title: Monorepo SDK Integrator Labs - local dev + telemetry sketch
summary: Lightweight hands-on lab for integrating the Redwood SDK into a large monorepo. Focus: fast local feedback loop, safe telemetry contracts, CI gating, and a minimal mock runtime for developer productivity.
content:
Purpose and audience:
This working doc is a lab-style quick reference for engineers who need to add Redwood SDK calls to an existing monorepo (frontend, backend, or fullstack services). It is intentionally opinionated: small, reproducible steps to get a working local flow, plus tests and telemetry contracts to prevent blast radius in CI. Target audience: platform engineers, SDK integrators, and senior fullstack devs doing initial integration work.

Design goals (why this lab exists):
- Local-first: get a round-trip without any hosted account or dedicated infra in <10 minutes.
- Safe telemetry: well-scoped event schema + validation so product analytics remains consistent.
- Fast CI feedback: compact contract tests that run on PRs (<= 2 minutes ideally).
- Minimal runtime parity: mock server that exercises typical call shapes (streaming, function-calls, embeddings).
- Low friction for monorepo constraints: work with workspaces (pnpm/turborepo/Nx) and existing lint/test pipelines.

Prereqs (assumptions in this lab):
- Local machine with node 18+, pnpm/yarn, Docker (optional but recommended), and GitHub Actions for CI.
- Monorepo uses workspace tooling (pnpm workspaces/turbo/Nx) and has a top-level scripts section.
- Developer has no hosted Redwood API key or prefers to avoid using it in early PRs.

Quick start steps (fast path):
1) Add the SDK package locally
   - At the repo root: pnpm add -w ./packages/redwood-sdk --save-dev OR use a path alias in package.json so the monorepo resolves the SDK package in-place.
   - Rationale: path install avoids published version bumps while iterating.

2) Install the local mock runtime (dev-only)
   - Create a tiny express server under tools/redwood-mock that implements three endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings, /v1/status.
   - Minimal behavior: return canned tokens for generate (simulate streaming by chunking with setTimeout), deterministic 1536-dim float32 arrays for embeddings, and a simple JSON with version+capabilities for /status.
   - Start script: pnpm --filter tools:redwood-mock start (provides a single local port to point SDK to).

3) Local env + feature flags
   - Add .env.dev.local (gitignored) with:
     REDWOOD_SDK_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4080
     REDWOOD_ENV=local
     REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_SENTRY_DSN=disabled
   - SDK should read REDWOOD_SDK_BASE_URL and prefer it in local mode.

4) Example usage snippet (backend service)
   - Insert an example wrapper in services/my-service/src/redwood-client.ts that exports two helpers: generateText(prompt, opts) and embedText(text).
   - Keep the wrapper synchronous-friendly: expose an async generator for streaming so existing handlers can pipe output incrementally.

5) Smoke test
   - Run tools/redwood-mock and execute a small integration test in the service: pnpm -w test --filter services/my-service -- test/integration/redwood-smoke.test.ts
   - The smoke test asserts: success response, a token stream with >3 chunks, and embedding vector length 1536.

Telemetry contract (core idea):
- Keep telemetry schema tiny and stable. Each SDK call emits at most one structured event for product analytics and one debug event for observability. Event fields: event_type, sdk_version, env, call_id (uuid), model_name (optional), latency_ms_bucket, success boolean.
- Example event (flattened JSON): {"event_type":"redwood.sdk.call","sdk_version":"0.5.0-local","env":"local","call_id":"...","model_name":"rwd-small-v1","latency_ms_bucket":"0-50","success":true}
- Validation: include a simple JSON schema under tools/telemetry/schemas/sdk-call-v1.json and a lightweight validator in CI that runs against recorded test events.

Contract tests (PR gating):
- Two categories: behavior contracts (SDK -> mock runtime) and telemetry contracts (event shape).
- Behavior contract test (fast): run a matrix of 3 canonical prompts and assert outputs contain expected markers (e.g., completion prefix, function call signature).
- Telemetry contract test (fast): run a short script that executes SDK calls and records emitted telemetry into a temp file; validate file against the schema, fail on missing required fields.
- CI placement: add a new job redwood-integration: runs on PRs for changes touching packages/redwood-sdk/**/* or services/**/* that import the SDK. Use path filters to avoid running on unrelated PRs.

Example GitHub Actions job (text only, insert in .github/workflows/ci.yml):
- name: Redwood SDK quick PR contract
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Setup Node
      uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with: node-version: 18
    - name: Install deps
      run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
    - name: Start mock runtime
      run: pnpm --filter tools:redwood-mock start & sleep 1
    - name: Run contract tests
      run: pnpm -w test --filter packages/redwood-sdk --tests redwood-contract.test.ts
  timeout-minutes: 12

Developer experience notes (pitfalls and antidotes):
- Long monorepo install times: prefer pnpm and a cached network store in CI. Provide a repo-level .npmrc and pnpm store layer in CI.
- Flaky tests from timing-dependent streaming: keep the mock streaming delays deterministic and slow enough to be realistic but generous to avoid race failures (e.g., 30ms chunk interval).
- Secrets leakage: ensure the mock runtime logs redact any environment-like values and the telemetry validator ignores ephemeral call_id values.

Rollout checklist (incremental integration approach):
1) Local lab: engineer integrates SDK with mock runtime and adds smoke tests.
2) PR: include behavior + telemetry contract tests.
3) Canary: merge to main with feature flag off; run a short e2e in staging pointing to a small hosted sandbox (optional).
4) Monitor: check telemetry event rates and any schema anomalies.
5) Flip: enable feature flag for production traffic on a small subset (5-10%) and continue to watch.

Notes on long-term hygiene (for platform team):
- Keep the mock runtime in tools/ and mark as dev-only in package.json (no publishes).
- Promote the telemetry schema to a shared schema repo when more than 3 product teams adopt it.
- Add a version header to all SDK events to allow non-breaking evolution.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- What dimension do we prefer for embedding vectors in the long run? (1536 chosen here as a safe default, but product teams may want smaller vectors for cost.)
- Do we accept a single company-wide telemetry schema or allow per-product extensions?
- Should the mock runtime support optional latency fuzzing to simulate tail latency in CI?

Next steps (short horizon):
- MVP: get one internal service fully integrated with smoke tests and telemetry validation within the week. Owner: Maya Chen (pair: Evan Mitchell).
- Follow-up: write a short internal demo walkthrough (5–7 minute screencast) demonstrating the local loop.

Appendix: useful snippets and conventions (copy-paste friendly)
- top-level package.json scripts:
  "scripts": {
    "start:redwood-mock": "node tools/redwood-mock/index.js",
    "test:redwood-contracts": "mocha packages/redwood-sdk/test/redwood-contract.test.ts --timeout 10000"
  }

- minimal mock response example (JSON for /v1/generate):
  {
    "id": "mock-12345",
    "object": "text_completion",
    "choices": [
      {"text_chunks": ["hello"," world","!"], "finish_reason":"length"}
    ]
  }

- quick validation command (local):
  pnpm -w test --filter packages/redwood-sdk --grep redwood-contract || true

This doc is intentionally terse — treat it as a lab checklist rather than a full-runbook. Add implementation notes directly in the tools/ folders as you iterate.
